1. COMPANY OVERVIEW

The West Mercia Chronicle (WMC), commonly referred to as the Chronicle, is a regional news publisher serving Worcestershire, Herefordshire, and the surrounding West Mercia area. The paper has been a continuous presence in the region since its founding, with a heritage of local reporting that spans multiple generations of readers and advertisers. Its editorial independence and commitment to community journalism remain the cornerstone of its operations.

The Chronicle operates from two principal offices: the main editorial and administrative hub at 14 Friar Street, Worcester, WR1 2NA, and a satellite newsroom in Hereford at 27 Commercial Road, Hereford, HR1 2BB. The Worcester office houses the senior editorial team, commercial sales, and corporate functions. The Hereford office serves as the base for the county reporting team and the weekly Herefordshire edition.

The newspaper’s mission is to provide accurate, balanced, and timely news coverage of the communities it serves, while supporting local businesses through advertising and partnership opportunities. The Chronicle also maintains a modest digital presence, with a website updated daily and a social media team operating across two platforms.

---

2. HISTORY AND HERITAGE

The West Mercia Chronicle was founded in 1887 as a weekly broadsheet serving the city of Worcester and its immediate environs. Its first edition, printed on a hand-operated press in a small back-street workshop, promised “a faithful record of local affairs, honestly reported and plainly written.” That promise remains the editorial charter under which the paper operates today.

West Mercia Chronicle founded_year 1887 year. Record status: current. This founding date is recorded in the company’s original articles of association, held in the Worcester office archive, and is the current official founding year used in all corporate communications and public records.

Over the decades, the Chronicle has weathered two world wars, the transition from hot metal to digital typesetting, and the consolidation of regional press ownership. It has remained independent, owned by the same family trust since 1923. The paper has won regional awards for investigative reporting in 1978, 1999, and 2015, and its archive of bound volumes from 1887 to the present day is one of the most complete local newspaper collections in the West Midlands.

A centenary supplement was published in 1987, and a 125th anniversary special edition was produced in 2012. Both are available for reference in the HR office and in the public reading room at the Worcester branch of the county library.

### 7.1 Digital Subscription Platform

The Chronicle will complete the migration of its digital subscription platform to the new content management system by 2026-03-31. The project, referred to internally as the "Digital First" programme, began in 2024-11 with an audit of legacy systems. The migration is being managed by the IT department in conjunction with the editorial production team.

A provisional budget of £185,000 has been allocated for the 2025–26 financial year, covering software licensing, staff training, and temporary contractor costs. A decision is expected by 2026-01-31. Staff consultation meetings were held on 2025-10-08 and 2025-10-15, and written submissions from staff were accepted until 2025-10-31. No final decision has been made as of the date of this directory.

### 7.3 Community News Fund

The Chronicle launched the Community News Fund in 2025-04 to support local journalism projects proposed by community groups and parish councils. The fund provides grants of up to £500 per project, with a total annual allocation of £10,000.

In the first funding round, which closed on 2025-06-30, the fund received 23 applications. Nine grants were awarded, with a total value of £3,950. The second funding round opened on 2025-10-01 and closes on 2025-12-15.

The fund is administered by the editorial department, and applications are reviewed by a panel comprising the editor, the deputy editor, and the community affairs correspondent. The panel's decisions are final and are announced in the newspaper and on the website.

### 7.4 Apprenticeship Programme

The Chronicle will recruit two journalism apprentices in 2026, with placements beginning in September 2026. The apprenticeships will be delivered in partnership with the National Council for the Training of Journalists (NCTJ) and will lead to a formal qualification in journalism.

The apprentices will be based at the Worcester head office for the first six months and will then rotate through the district offices in Hereford, Kidderminster, and Leominster. Each apprentice will be assigned a mentor from the senior editorial team.

Applications will open on 2026-01-05 and close on 2026-02-27. The recruitment process will include a written assessment and an interview. The company is committed to ensuring that the recruitment process is open and transparent, and applications are welcomed from candidates of all backgrounds.

### 7.5 Environmental Sustainability Commitments

The board adopted an environmental sustainability policy on 2025-03-20. The policy commits the company to:

- Reducing print waste by 15% by 2027-12-31, compared with the 2024 baseline.
- Switching the company vehicle fleet to hybrid or electric vehicles by 2028-12-31, subject to the availability of suitable vehicles and charging infrastructure.
- Sourcing 50% of the electricity used at the Worcester head office from renewable sources by 2026-06-30.

WEST MERCIA CHRONICLE
Corporate Records and Staff Directory

1. COMPANY OVERVIEW

The West Mercia Chronicle (WMC), commonly referred to as the Chronicle, is a regional news publisher serving Worcestershire, Herefordshire, and the surrounding West Mercia area. The paper has been a continuous presence in the region since its founding, with a heritage of local reporting that spans multiple generations of readers and advertisers. Its editorial independence and commitment to community journalism remain the cornerstone of its operations.

The Chronicle operates from two principal offices: the main editorial and administrative hub at 14 Friar Street, Worcester, WR1 2NA, and a satellite newsroom in Hereford at 27 Commercial Road, Hereford, HR1 2BB. The Worcester office houses the senior editorial team, commercial sales, and corporate functions. The Hereford office serves as the base for the county reporting team and the weekly Herefordshire edition.

The newspaper’s mission is to provide accurate, balanced, and timely news coverage of the communities it serves, while supporting local businesses through advertising and partnership opportunities. The Chronicle also maintains a modest digital presence, with a website updated daily and a social media team operating across two platforms.

---

2. HISTORY AND HERITAGE

The West Mercia Chronicle was founded in 1887 as a weekly broadsheet serving the city of Worcester and its immediate environs. Its first edition, printed on a hand-operated press in a small back-street workshop, promised “a faithful record of local affairs, honestly reported and plainly written.” That promise remains the editorial charter under which the paper operates today.

West Mercia Chronicle founded_year 1887 year. Record status: current. This founding date is recorded in the company’s original articles of association, held in the Worcester office archive, and is the current official founding year used in all corporate communications and public records.

Over the decades, the Chronicle has weathered two world wars, the transition from hot metal to digital typesetting, and the consolidation of regional press ownership. It has remained independent, owned by the same family trust since 1923. The paper has won regional awards for investigative reporting in 1978, 1999, and 2015, and its archive of bound volumes from 1887 to the present day is one of the most complete local newspaper collections in the West Midlands.

A centenary supplement was published in 1987, and a 125th anniversary special edition was produced in 2012. Both are available for reference in the HR office and in the public reading room at the Worcester branch of the county library.

---

3. OFFICE LOCATIONS AND FACILITIES

3.1 Worcester Office (Head Office)
Address: 14 Friar Street, Worcester, WR1 2NA
Telephone: 01905 612345
Facilities: Open-plan newsroom (capacity 40), meeting rooms (3), HR office, finance department, print coordination desk, staff kitchen, secure bicycle storage.
Access hours: 08:00–18:00, Monday to Friday; 09:00–13:00 on Saturdays during the winter season. The building is locked outside these hours, and staff requiring access must hold a valid security fob.

3.2 Hereford Office (Satellite)
Address: 27 Commercial Road, Hereford, HR1 2BB
Telephone: 01432 276543
Facilities: Newsroom (capacity 12), shared meeting space, two interview rooms, small photographic studio.
Access hours: 09:00–17:00, Monday to Friday. The Hereford office operates on a hot-desking arrangement, and staff are expected to book desks in advance through the internal booking system.

Both offices are equipped with a backup power supply and a dedicated fibre connection. The Worcester office has a generator that can sustain the full newsroom for up to six hours in the event of a power cut; the Hereford office has a smaller uninterruptible power supply that covers essential servers and telephony only.

## 6. Office Locations and Operational Changes

### 6.1 Main Office – Worcester

The Chronicle's head office is located at:

**West Mercia Chronicle**
**14–18 Severn Street**
**Worcester WR1 2AB**

The building houses the editorial, advertising, marketing, accounts, and administration departments, together with the publisher's office and the boardroom. The premises are leased from Severn Street Properties (Worcester) Ltd under a lease that runs until 2032, with a break clause at the five-year point. The landlord has been advised of the Chronicle's intention to exercise the break clause, and the property team are currently in discussion with two potential replacement tenants. No formal notice has yet been served.

The Severn Street office has a small staff car park to the rear, with 22 marked spaces. Parking is allocated on a first-come, first-served basis, except for the four spaces reserved for the Editor, the Publisher, the Deputy Editor, and the Advertising Director. A waiting list for the remaining spaces is maintained by the Facilities Office; as of the date of this directory, there are 14 staff on the list. Staff who do not have a car park space are advised to use the city centre multi-storey car parks, and the Chronicle reimburses the cost of parking permits for staff who regularly attend the office.

### 6.2 Worcester City Centre Office (Closed)

The former city centre office at 3–5 The Cross was closed on 2023-03-31. The lease was surrendered to the landlord, and the premises are now occupied by a coffee shop. All staff who were based at The Cross were relocated to Severn Street. The telephone number for the old office (01905 611000) was disconnected on 2023-04-14. The main switchboard number for Severn Street is 01905 611111.

### 6.3 Malvern Office (Closed)

The Malvern office at 22 Church Street, Malvern WR14 2AA, was closed on 2019-12-20. This office previously served as a base for the southern area field sales team and for the Malvern and Upton-upon-Severn district reporter. Since the closure, the southern area field sales representative (currently James Harding) has been home-based, and the district reporter is based at Severn Street and attends the Malvern area as required. The Malvern office telephone number (01684 572200) is no longer in service.

### 6.4 Kidderminster Office

The Kidderminster office at 9–11 Vicar Street, Kidderminster DY10 1DB, remains open and houses the Wyre Forest district editorial team and the northern area field sales team. The office has a public reception desk, which is staffed between 9:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m., Monday to Friday. The office is leased from Kidderminster Commercial Holdings Ltd, with the lease due for renewal on 2026-06-24. The Chronicle's property team has indicated that the lease will be renewed for a further five years, subject to agreement on the rent.

The Kidderminster office has a staff car park with 12 spaces. The spaces are allocated by the district office manager, and there is currently no waiting list.

### 6.5 Leominster Office

The Leominster office at 5 Corn Square, Leominster HR6 8LR, is a small satellite office used by the North Herefordshire district reporter and by the field sales representative covering the north-west of the circulation area. The office has a shared reception desk with the Leominster Tourist Information Centre, and the Chronicle pays a contribution towards the shared costs. The arrangement is governed by a service level agreement dated 2021-09-01, which is reviewed annually.

The Leominster office does not have a staff car park. Staff based there use the public car park opposite the office, and the Chronicle reimburses the cost of parking permits.

### 6.6 Tenbury Wells Office (Closed)

The Tenbury Wells office at 12 Market Street, Tenbury Wells WR15 8HN, was closed on 2018-08-31. The office had been used by the district reporter for the Tenbury area, and the closure followed the retirement of the then district reporter. The Tenbury area is now covered by the district reporter based at Leominster. The lease on the Market Street premises was not renewed, and the property was returned to the landlord on 2018-09-14.

## 7. FUTURE INITIATIVES AND COMPANY OUTLOOK

The following section summarises planned developments and strategic priorities as recorded at the time of the 2025 annual review. Items marked *provisional* are subject to board approval or external agreement and should not be treated as committed expenditure.

### 7.1 Digital Subscription Platform

The Chronicle will complete the migration of its digital subscription platform to the new content management system by 2026-03-31. The project, referred to internally as the "Digital First" programme, began in 2024-11 with an audit of legacy systems. The migration is being managed by the IT department in conjunction with the editorial production team.

A provisional budget of £185,000 has been allocated for the 2025–26 financial year, covering software licensing, staff training, and temporary contractor costs. The board approved the budget at its meeting on 2025-05-14, with the condition that the project delivers measurable growth in digital-only subscriptions by the end of the second quarter of 2026.

The current digital subscriber base stands at 4,280 accounts as of 2025-09-30. The target for 2026-12-31 is 6,000 accounts. Progress against this target will be reported to the board on a quarterly basis.

### 7.2 Worcester City Centre Office Relocation

The company has entered into a period of consultation regarding the possible relocation of the Worcester city centre office. The current lease on the Trinity Street premises expires on 2026-09-30, and the landlord has indicated that the rent will increase by approximately 18% upon renewal.

Three options are under consideration:

1. Renew the existing lease at the increased rent.
2. Relocate to smaller premises at 4 The Butts, Worcester WR1 3PA, with a lease term of five years.
3. Consolidate the Worcester editorial team into the Malvern office and operate a reduced city centre presence through a shared workspace arrangement.

A decision is expected by 2026-01-31. Staff consultation meetings were held on 2025-10-08 and 2025-10-15, and written submissions from staff were accepted until 2025-10-31. No final decision has been made as of the date of this directory.

### 7.3 Community News Fund

The Chronicle launched the Community News Fund in 2025-04 to support local journalism projects proposed by community groups and parish councils. The fund provides grants of up to £500 per project, with a total annual allocation of £10,000.

In the first funding round, which closed on 2025-06-30, the fund received 23 applications. Nine grants were awarded, with a total value of £3,950. The second funding round opened on 2025-10-01 and closes on 2025-12-15.

The fund is administered by the editorial department, and applications are reviewed by a panel comprising the editor, the deputy editor, and the community affairs correspondent. The panel's decisions are final and are announced in the newspaper and on the website.

### 7.4 Apprenticeship Programme

The Chronicle will recruit two journalism apprentices in 2026, with placements beginning in September 2026. The apprenticeships will be delivered in partnership with the National Council for the Training of Journalists (NCTJ) and will lead to a formal qualification in journalism.

The apprentices will be based at the Worcester head office for the first six months and will then rotate through the district offices in Hereford, Kidderminster, and Leominster. Each apprentice will be assigned a mentor from the senior editorial team.

Applications will open on 2026-01-05 and close on 2026-02-27. The recruitment process will include a written assessment and an interview. The company is committed to ensuring that the recruitment process is open and transparent, and applications are welcomed from candidates of all backgrounds.

### 7.5 Environmental Sustainability Commitments

The board adopted an environmental sustainability policy on 2025-03-20. The policy commits the company to:

- Reducing print waste by 15% by 2027-12-31, compared with the 2024 baseline.
- Switching the company vehicle fleet to hybrid or electric vehicles by 2028-12-31, subject to the availability of suitable vehicles and charging infrastructure.
- Sourcing 50% of the electricity used at the Worcester head office from renewable sources by 2026-06-30.
